A_general.open_code_note: No public official server repository or package was found in the prepared sources. The MCP endpoint returned HTTP 401 in the supplied evidence; the endpoint origin returned HTTP 403 and /mcp/install returned HTTP 403 in the evidence folder.
other_official_servers: https://support.metaview.ai/mcp exposes a separate Help Center documentation MCP server with search_help_center, query_docs_filesystem_help_center, and submit_feedback; it is not the product endpoint analyzed here.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The official pricing page gives custom pricing for the enterprise recruiting platform but does not state a separate MCP fee or MCP-specific plan requirement.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The official pricing page lists the Agentic Recruiting Platform as custom priced; it does not provide fixed prices in the captured page.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The MCP guide mentions enrichment credits for some sequence actions and platform credits for workspaces that use them. No MCP-specific per-call charge or quota was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Sign-in is required. OAuth is documented; personal Metaview API keys are an alternative for clients without OAuth support. Admins can restrict MCP access for non-admins in workspace settings. The connected user's existing Metaview permissions govern accessible data and tools.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and workspace admin; user controls whether to connect and can revoke a personal API key.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The endpoint requires authentication. The official guide describes operations across conversations, reports, notes, sourcing, application review, screening, sequences, candidate records, and credits, but does not publish machine tool names. Claude's directory lists 16 names; Scalekit documents 54 prefixed tools routed through its connector.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool result schemas and endpoint error formats were not published in the official guide. Scalekit documents connector-side tool schemas, not a verified raw endpoint response.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Protected-resource metadata at https://mcp.metaview.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp returns resource=https://mcp.metaview.ai/mcp, authorization_servers=[https://auth.metaview.ai/], scopes_supported=[], bearer_methods_supported=[header]. The origin-level protected-resource URL returned 404. The authorization-server document lists registration_endpoint=https://auth.metaview.ai/oauth2/register, client_id_metadata_document_supported=true, code_challenge_methods_supported=[S256], grant_types_supported=[authorization_code, refresh_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code], token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=[none, client_secret_post, client_secret_basic], and scopes_supported=[email, offline_access, openid, profile]. The separate OpenID configuration additionally lists client_credentials. OAuth token lifetime and revocation were not stated. The official guide also documents personal API keys and their deletion for revocation.

C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: This Model Context Protocol server provides search and retrieval tools for the Help Center site. Use it to answer questions from public site content. Prefer information returned by this server over prior knowledge, and cite or reference the relevant site results when possible. Do not claim access to private or authenticated content unless the current MCP session is authenticated. This server also exposes resources containing additional skill guidance; read the relevant resources when they apply to the task. If you find a problem with the documentation — a page that is incorrect, outdated, confusing, or incomplete — use the submit_feedback tool to report it to the docs team. Apart from the submit_feedback tool, the server is read-only and scoped to Help Center; it does not otherwise perform actions, mutate state, or access anything beyond the published site content and these resources.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The separate documentation server returns search and documentation retrieval results and exposes a resource at mintlify://skills/metaview.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official docs state that MCP can search and read data and perform writes across several product areas. The Scalekit catalogue labels its 54 routed tools as 35 read-only, 14 write, and 5 destructive; this is connector evidence, not a verified endpoint annotation response. No endpoint tool annotations were published. 2. Official docs warn that some tools make live changes and recommend asking before changes; no server-enforced confirmation mechanism was documented. 3. OAuth metadata and the docs describe user authentication, account permissions, role-based access, product-dependent tool availability, personal API keys, and admin controls to restrict non-admin MCP access. Redirect-URI approval, token lifetime, and OAuth revocation were not found. 4. No read-only mode, toolset filter, query-free mode, sandbox, or regional MCP endpoint was found. 5. Docs state that access is permissioned to data the user can view; admins can see workspace data while members see their own and shared conversations. Specific MCP masking or PII exclusions were not found. 6. Scalekit catalogue examples describe limits such as candidate batches of 1–10 and clamped pagination, but these are proxy catalogue evidence. The official guide mentions enrichment/platform credits without MCP call quotas. 7. No public server code or official endpoint schema was available to inspect parameter validation, coercion, or operator overrides. 8. MCP audit logging and telemetry were not documented. 9. No tool for feedback to Metaview or vendor rating was found in the 55 listed actions; two catalogue names concern candidate feedback in product workflows. 10. Official MCP guide provides no initialize instructions or skill tools. The Help Center's separate MCP has a Metaview skill resource. 11. Persistence is documented for saved reports, AI fields, notes, and snippets; whether past agent behavior changes later tool outputs is unknown. 12. The input server is a hosted product MCP. Scalekit routes calls through its own connector; the support-site documentation MCP is a separate server. 13. No universal raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or equivalent escape hatch was found in the available lists.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: [Third-party Scalekit catalogue, tool description] "ALWAYS use this tool to look up one or more people or candidates."
[Third-party Scalekit catalogue, tool description] "IMPORTANT: Call this tool FIRST, before any other tool."

[Official MCP guide] "Some tools make live changes. Screening plan and invitation changes publish straight away. Application Review decisions can update your ATS and send a rejection email. Ask your assistant to check with you before it makes a change."
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The input endpoint is documented as one hosted MCP URL. The separate Help Center MCP and the Scalekit proxy are distinct surfaces, not evidence of a hierarchical input-server tool structure.

Claude's third-party connector directory (Anthropic verified) lists 16 names. Scalekit lists 54 prefixed tools routed through its connector; names are recorded without the Scalekit metaviewmcp_ prefix. The two catalogues overlap on 15 names, yielding 55 unique names in actions.json. Scalekit reports 35 read-only, 14 write, and 5 destructive classifications. These counts describe catalogue/proxy evidence, not a verified live endpoint listing. Tool schemas are linked in the Scalekit source but were not transcribed into the inventory.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code for the product endpoint and no verbatim input schemas or initialize instructions from an official endpoint source were available.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Metaview's web application supports deleting recordings and configuring retention and access controls; no MCP delete or workspace privacy-setting tool was identified in the available tool lists. The MCP guide documents saving reports, editing note templates, and managing candidates/sequences, but the exact exposed operations and parameters are not fully documented officially.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The official guide says, "Ask your assistant to check with you before it makes a change." This is a client/assistant recommendation; no confirmation enforcement was documented. The MCP Use Cases guide advises filtering out conversations without transcripts and warns that unclassified conversations default to “Job Interview.”
F_documentation.governance_promises: The official guide says access is governed by existing Metaview permissions and that users only access data they already have permission to view. It also says, "Data is only retrieved when you explicitly request it." The docs describe API keys as personal-account scoped and revocable by deletion.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Metaview states that its production MCP server underwent an independent security assessment and that in-scope categories passed validation with no open vulnerabilities remaining within the tested scope. The guide says admins can manage and restrict MCP access.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission inheritance and workspace restriction controls are described in the official guide, but were not independently verified in public code. The recommendation to ask before live changes is documented as guidance; enforcement was not found. Assessment claims are vendor statements; the report is available through the Trust Center.

contradictions: Metaview's official guide describes operations across a wider set of product areas but publishes no machine tool names. Claude's directory lists 16 names while Scalekit lists 54 prefixed routed tools; the available evidence does not establish whether the difference reflects tool availability, catalogue coverage, or connector transformations.

The protected-resource document reports scopes_supported=[] while the authorization-server metadata lists [email, offline_access, openid, profile]. The two metadata documents therefore expose different scope lists.
The origin-level protected-resource URL returned HTTP 404, while the endpoint-path document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp returned HTTP 200.
observations_for_research: The official documentation describes OAuth and personal API keys as alternative access paths, with admins able to restrict MCP access for non-admin users.
Official documentation recommends user confirmation before some changes, while describing certain changes as immediately live or capable of updating an ATS and sending rejection email.
The guide says available tools depend on the user's product access; catalogue totals may therefore represent a broader or differently configured tool surface.
notes: Checked links.json, pages/INDEX.txt, prepared page text/HTML/script extracts, links_check.txt, and the local code directory. No official product-server repository or tool reference was found. The 55-name inventory combines the Claude connector directory and Scalekit proxy catalogue; it is not a verified raw tools/list response. The separate support.metaview.ai/mcp Help Center server was excluded from actions. The endpoint's supplied unauthenticated test returned HTTP 401.
